title: Replication of Intra-Model Repetition Across Temporal Sessions

original_idea.title: Replication of Intra-Model Repetition Across Temporal Sessions
original_idea.problem: It is unknown whether intra-model repetition persists across temporal sessions, which would indicate systemic persistence rather than a run-time artifact.
original_idea.direction: Re-run a fixed set of probes from Infinity-Chat on the same model API endpoints at 30-day intervals over 3-6 months and track similarity scores.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Temporal persistence of homogeneity would indicate that the problem is architectural and training-based rather than correctable through inference-time parameters.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind documents intra-model repetition but does not track temporal stability. This directly follows up on finding (a).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: temporal persistence is informative for understanding the root cause, but it doesn't directly improve safety outcomes.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: re-running probes at intervals and tracking similarity scores is straightforward and requires only API calls and basic analysis.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No clear milestone: the project requires 3-6 months of data collection at 30-day intervals, far exceeding the 30-hour timeframe constraint.

novelty.reasoning: Existing work studies LLM output consistency across immediate repeated runs, but no study tracks the Artificial Hivemind intra-model repetition metric across temporal sessions (weeks/months). The LLM stability literature focuses on benchmark accuracy variation, not on the persistence of the specific repetition patterns identified by the Hivemind paper.

evidence.source: LLM Stability: A detailed analysis with some surprises (arXiv 2408.04667)
evidence.finding: Studies LLM output stability across runs, finding accuracy variations of up to 10% across identical runs for deterministically configured LLMs.
